title: 26.4 A 24-to-29GHz Compact Transmit/Receive Front-End Module Featuring an Asymmetric Doherty Power Amplifier and 0.22mm2 Area
problem: Mm-wave FEMs must simultaneously achieve high TX linearity/efficiency and low RX noise figure while remaining compact. Conventional Class-AB PAs provide <10% TX PAE under OFDM signals with 10dB PAPR, limiting overall system efficiency.
motivation: mm-Wave beamformer performance critically depends on compact, efficient FEM design; 5G and higher frequencies demand better TX efficiency while maintaining low noise and tight footprint.
method: An asymmetric Doherty power amplifier (DPA) design provides high efficiency under modulated signals through dynamic bias adjustment and impedance modulation. The FEM integrates PA, LNA, and T/R switch in a 0.22mm² footprint for 24-29GHz operation.
key_novelty: Asymmetric Doherty PA architecture achieving high PAE under OFDM waveforms while maintaining compact integration in a small FEM form factor.
contributions: Compact FEM in 0.22mm² total area for 24-29GHz operation
Asymmetric Doherty PA improving TX efficiency vs. conventional Class-AB
Integrated PA, LNA, and T/R switch for simplified beamformer design
Demonstrates improved PAE under realistic OFDM signal conditions
limitations: Not discussed; linearity and thermal stability under sustained operation not fully characterized.
primary_theme: Asymmetric Doherty PA for compact mm-wave FEMs
